The sharp market rally following the election was the ideal setup to start looking at short positions. It reminds me of what legendary market analyst Richard Ney used to warn about decades ago regarding how specialists operate on Wall Street. Ney documented how market makers routinely use artificially engineered rallies and post event euphoria to create liquidity. That spike in volume allows institutional insiders to unload their inventory onto retail buyers at top dollar right before the narrative shifts. What we saw over the last two days fits that classic distribution playbook perfectly. Once you strip away the headline hype, these sudden surges are often less about genuine long term economic expansion and much more about large institutions clearing out their books at the expense of retail traders rushing in at the top.
